sections.title: Ptosis: Comprehensive Clinical Assessment
content: 1. Inspection: Check for bilateral/unilateral ptosis, frontalis overaction, lid crease height, dermatochalasis, squint, anisocoria, heterochromia, and scars.
2. Preparation: Clean hands and obtain patient permission.
3. Primary Measurements: Evaluate Palpebral fissure height, MRD1, MRD2, Levator function, and Upper lid crease height.
4. Dynamic Tests: Examine EOM, check for Marcus Gunn jaw winking (moving jaw side to side), and Myasthenia (look up for 30-60 sec).
5. Eyelid Signs: Check for Cogan twitch (look rapidly from downgaze to primary), Bell phenomena, and Lagophthalmos.
6. Surface Health: Examine tear film (height and instability).

sections.title: Complications & Indications for Repair
content: Intraoperative: Hemorrhage, Globe injury.
Early Postop: Hematoma, Infection, Exposure Keratopathy, Lagophthalmos, Contour defect.
Late Postop: Recurrence, Contralateral lid ptosis (Hering's Law).
Indications: Visual field obstruction (covering pupil), Brow headache, Chin-up posture, Cosmetic concerns.

sections.title: Blepharophimosis Ptosis Syndrome (BPES)
content: Diagnosis: Bilateral ptosis, absent lid crease, Telecanthus, Epicanthus inversus, Nasal bridge hypoplasia.
Complications: Amblyopia is the most worrisome (present in 50%).
Workup: VA, Refraction, Pupils, EOM, Bell's, Marcus Gunn exclusion.
Management Order: 1. Refraction/Amblyopia Rx. 2. Telecanthus/Epicanthus repair. 3. Ptosis repair (Brow suspension). 4. Ectropion repair (teens).

sections.title: Ectropion: Classification & Findings
content: Clinical Findings: Outward turning margin, inflamed/thickened/keratinized conjunctiva, periorbital fat prolapse.
Acquired Types: Involutional (age), Cicatricial (scar), Paralytic (CN VII palsy), Mechanical (tumors), Iatrogenic (over-correction).
Horizontal Laxity: Eyelid distraction test (>6mm) and Eyelid snap test (failure to spring back without blink).
Canthal Laxity: Medial (Punctum reaches limbus/pupil on lateral traction); Lateral (Round appearance, medially pulls >2mm).

sections.title: Hertel Exophthalmometry Technique
sections.content: The device measures distance from the lateral orbital rim to the corneal apex using mirrors at 45 degrees. Place notches on the bony lateral rim using the smallest base possible. sections.title: Management of Pediatric Masses
content: Main concerns: Infection (Cellulitis) vs. Tumor (Rhabdomyosarcoma).
Workup: VA, EOM, Pupils, IOP, Fundus, CT/MRI, Incisional biopsy.
Treatment: Chemotherapy (Vincristine, Dactinomycin, Cyclophosphamide), Radiotherapy, Surgical debulking, Exenteration (recurrent).
Prognosis: 90% survival if confined to the bony orbit.

sections.title: Congenital Nasolacrimal Duct Obstruction
content: 1. Dye Disappearance Test (DDT): Instill Fluorescein; Evaluate at 5 min. Grade 0 (None) to 3 (Wide/bright/spillage).
2. Conservative (Year 1): Crigler Massage, Antibiotics for conjunctivitis (avoid for white eye), Systemic ABx for Dacryocystitis.
3. Surgical (Year 1+): Syringing and Probing (90% success). Advance probe to nasal bone, rotate 90°, breach distal membrane ('pop').
4. Patency Confirmation: Metal-on-metal contact, Saline irrigation (swallow reflex/aspiration), Direct observation.
5. Failure Management: NLD Intubation with silicone stents, then DCR.

sections.title: Malignant Eyelid Lesions: SCC & BCC
content: DDx: Preseptal cellulitis, Chalazion, SCC, BCC, SGC, Melanoma, Merkel Cell.
Surgical Margins: 2-4 mm for small BCC; 5 mm for large BCC, SCC, SGC, and Melanoma.
Sebaceous Gland Carcinoma (SGC): requires Map Biopsies (4 quadrants + tarsal conjunctiva) and Oil Red O stain. Watch for skip lesions.
Regional Spread: Check Sentinel Lymph Nodes. MRI/CT for perineural invasion or intracranial spread.
Adjuvant: Topical Imiquimod/Interferon (elderly), Cryotherapy (map biopsy positive), Radiotherapy (second-best).

sections.title: Eyelid Coloboma & Orbital Floor Fractures
content: Coloboma: Associated with Goldenhar or Amniotic band syndrome. Repaired via direct closure or semicircular flaps. Avoid lid-sharing in infants (amblyopia risk).
Orbital Fracture Findings: Inferior dystopia, enophthalmos, pseudoptosis, crepitus, infraorbital hypesthesia.
Entrapment: Restricted motility + Positive Forced Duction Test = Muscle/fat entrapment.
Management: Conservative (edema reduction). Surgery if Enophthalmos >2mm, primary diplopia, or cosmetic defect.
